evidence.quote:
will and consciousness are
stronger than organic life itself, so that if a bodily frame be
but originally healthy and carefully preserved, it may through a
scientific enhancement of these qualities retain a kind of nervous
animation despite the most serious impairments, defects, or even
absences in the battery of specific organs
evidence.paraphrase: Muñoz explains his theory that willpower and consciousness can sustain a preserved body even when specific organs fail.

evidence.quote:
the frigidity of his
habitation--some fifty-five or fifty-six degrees Fahrenheit--was
maintained by an absorption system of ammonia cooling, the gasoline
engine whose pumps I had often heard in my room below
evidence.paraphrase: The cold of Muñoz's room is maintained by an ammonia-absorption refrigeration system driven by a gasoline engine.

evidence.quote:
he did not scorn
the incantations of the medi fffe6valists, since he believed these cryptic
formul fffe6 to contain rare psychological stimuli which might conceivably
have singular effects on the substance of a nervous system from which
organic pulsations had fled
evidence.paraphrase: Muñoz used medieval incantations, believing them to be psychological stimuli affecting a nervous system that no longer had organic function.

evidence.quote:
his demands for cold air increased, and with my aid he amplified the
ammonia piping of his room and modified the pumps and feed of his
refrigerating machine until he could keep the temperature as low as
thirty-four or forty degrees, and finally even twenty-eight degrees
evidence.paraphrase: Over time Muñoz progressively lowers his room's temperature to below freezing to sustain himself.

evidence.quote:
One night about eleven the pump of the
refrigerating machine broke down, so that within three hours the
process of ammonia cooling became impossible
evidence.paraphrase: The refrigeration pump fails, ending the cooling process that keeps Muñoz preserved.

evidence.quote:
There are
things about which it is better not to speculate, and all
that I can say is that I hate the smell of ammonia, and grow faint at a
draft of unusually cool air
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator retains a lasting revulsion to ammonia and cool air after the events.

evidence.quote:
I fancy you know--what I said about the will and the nerves and the
preserved body after the organs ceased to work. It was good theory, but
couldn't keep up indefinitely. There was a gradual deterioration I had
not foreseen.
evidence.paraphrase: Muñoz's note admits that his method of will-based preservation eventually failed through unforeseen deterioration.

evidence.quote:
for you
see I died that time eighteen years ago
evidence.paraphrase: The final revelation that Muñoz had actually died eighteen years earlier and been artificially preserved.

evidence.quote:
as I saw Doctor Mu fff1oz in that blast of cool air, I felt
a repugnance which nothing in his aspect could justify
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator feels an unexplained repugnance toward Muñoz on first meeting.

evidence.quote:
It had to be done my way--artificial preservation--_for you
see I died that time eighteen years ago_
evidence.paraphrase: Muñoz reveals his condition was maintained by artificial preservation after his death eighteen years prior.
